draft.title: Explicit and implicit memory
card: is recalled on purpose. You know you are remembering. It covers facts and personal events, such as the capital of Western Australia or your last birthday.
shows in what you do, without trying to recall it. It covers skills, such as riding a bike, and conditioned responses, such as feeling anxious at the sound of a dentist's drill.
A simple test is to ask whether the person is deliberately recalling the information. If they are, the memory is explicit. If it shows in their actions or reactions, it is implicit.
A person can use both at once. A pianist deliberately recalls the name of a piece, while their fingers play it without thought.
draft.remember: Explicit memory is deliberately recalled. Implicit memory shows in what you do.

a.q: Which is an example of an implicit memory?
opts: Tying your shoelaces without thinking about the steps
Listing the planets in order for a quiz
Describing what you did on your last holiday
Stating the date of a school excursion
a.why: Tying shoelaces is a skill that shows in action, with no deliberate recall. The other three involve deliberately recalling facts or events, so they are explicit.
a.clue: Which one happens without trying to remember?

b.q: Tom was bitten by a dog as a child. Now his heart races whenever he hears barking, though he cannot recall the bite. What does this show?
opts: An implicit memory, shown as a conditioned response
An explicit memory, because it is about a past event
An explicit memory, because it affects his body
An implicit memory, because it is a fact he knows
b.why: His reaction shows in what his body does, and he is not deliberately recalling anything, so it is implicit. The event is tempting as explicit, but he cannot recall it on purpose.

a.best: Tying your shoelaces without thinking about the steps

b.best: An implicit memory, shown as a conditioned response

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and is the only one with a qualifier, 'without thinking about the steps', which echoes the card's definition of implicit memory. A student could pick it without knowing the idea.
